headline.headline: PIRATES COMPLETE DOUBLEHEADER SPLIT AT THE STADIUM, STEAL SERIES LEAD IN TEN
headline.deck: Pittsburgh wins wild nightcap in extra innings after Yankees take the afternoon game
headline.body:
NEW YORK — The Pittsburgh Pirates arrived at Yankee Stadium on Wednesday for a doubleheader and left the Bronx with something far more valuable than a split: a series lead. After dropping the afternoon game 2-1, the Pirates rallied in the nightcap to beat the Yankees 5-3 in ten innings before 43,290 fans, with relief pitcher G. Soto earning the win in a game that did not break open until extra frames.

The nightcap was scoreless through four innings before Pittsburgh scratched across two runs in the fifth. The Yankees answered with three in the seventh to seize the lead, setting up a tense finish. The Pirates pushed two across in the tenth off a Yankees bullpen that had nothing left to give, and Soto slammed the door in the bottom half to seal it. A. Wells was hit by a pitch from M. Keller during the contest, a small subplot in a game filled with tension. The final time of game was 3:10, nearly an hour longer than the swift afternoon contest.

In the day game, the Yankees needed just 2 hours and 25 minutes to dispatch Pittsburgh 2-0, with both runs coming in the seventh inning. Cody Bellinger and a batter identified in the notes as Dominguez each doubled in the game. Despite that loss, the Pirates now hold the upper hand in the series heading into Thursday, a remarkable turn given they made the trip to the most famous address in baseball as the visiting underdog.

secondary.headline: RED SOX, ORIOLES SPLIT AS BALTIMORE BELLO HITS THREE BATTERS IN ROUGH OUTING
secondary.deck: Boston takes game one big, but Baltimore bounces back to even the series
secondary.body:
BOSTON — Fenway Park hosted a split doubleheader Wednesday that featured one lopsided opener and a comeback nightcap. The Red Sox stormed out to a 4-0 lead after the first inning in game one and held on to win 6-3, with starter Bennett earning the win. A home run was among the highlights for Boston in a contest that lasted just 2 hours and 19 minutes before 35,039 fans.

The nightcap told a different story. Baltimore's starter Ed Rivera was credited with the win as the Orioles raced to a 4-0 first-inning advantage and survived to win 5-1. Red Sox starter Bello had a rough go of it, hitting both T. Ward and Gunnar Henderson with pitches. Wilfredo Contreras was hit twice in the game, once by Bradish and once by T. Wells, making it a bruising afternoon for Baltimore's designated hitter. The Orioles, sitting at 50-50 entering play, took the split and headed into Thursday all square.

secondary.headline: ROYALS WALK OFF IN SEVENTH TO EDGE GIANTS, 5-4
secondary.deck: Kansas City starter S. Lugo picks up the win despite hitting Gilbert in a thriller
secondary.body:
KANSAS CITY — The Kansas City Royals scratched their way to a 5-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Wednesday at Kauffman Stadium, delivering the decisive blow in a five-run seventh inning that erased a deficit and stunned the visitors. S. Lugo earned the win for Kansas City despite hitting Giants batter Gilbert with a pitch during the contest. The game took just 2 hours and 12 minutes before an announced crowd of 14,606.

The Giants had held a 1-0 lead entering the seventh before the Royals erupted for five runs to take command. San Francisco added a run in the ninth to close within one, but Kansas City's bullpen held. The victory positions the Royals at 43-60 heading into a Thursday matchup against the Detroit Tigers, a team they will need to keep pace with in the muddled AL Central standings.

secondary.headline: SEAHAWKS SAFETY EMMANWORI ANKLE SURGERY A BUMP, NOT A CRISIS
secondary.deck: Seattle expects standout defensive back ready for Week 1 despite summer camp absence
secondary.body:
SEATTLE — Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori underwent ankle surgery and will miss a portion of training camp, the team confirmed Wednesday, though Seattle expects the standout defensive back to be healthy and ready for the regular season opener. The news tempers what would otherwise be a quiet offseason for a franchise looking to rebuild its defensive identity around the young safety.

Emmanwori emerged as one of the more promising defensive players at his position during the 2025 season, and his absence from early camp reps is not ideal for a unit installing new concepts. Still, the timetable suggests the Seahawks dodged a significant bullet. Elsewhere around the NFL, quarterbacks continue to be shuffled as rosters take shape, with Jaxon Dart drawing attention as a dark-horse starter worth monitoring heading into the summer.

column.headline: THE PIRATES JUST WALKED INTO THE STADIUM AND TOOK SOMETHING
column.body:
There is a moment in every baseball season when a team tells you who it is. For the Pittsburgh Pirates, that moment came Wednesday night in the Bronx, when they dropped a doubleheader opener, regrouped between games, and then grinded through ten innings to steal the nightcap in a ballpark that has buried lesser clubs for a century. That is not a lucky bounce. That is a team that does not flinch.

The Yankees, playing at home before crowds north of 40,000, could not finish off a Pittsburgh club that has no business winning in that building on paper. G. Soto got the final outs. The Pirates scored two in the tenth when the Yankees needed a clean inning most. Winning a series opener at Yankee Stadium is the kind of thing you remember in October. Pittsburgh may not be a pennant contender yet, but after Wednesday night, nobody in that clubhouse is pretending to be a tourist either.

story.headline: PIRATES STUN YANKEES IN TEN, TAKE SERIES OPENER AT THE STADIUM
story.deck: Pittsburgh scores twice in extras to complete comeback win before 43,290
story.body:
NEW YORK — The Pittsburgh Pirates were four outs from being shut out at Yankee Stadium when the night turned in their favor. Trailing 3-2 heading into the 10th inning on Wednesday, Pittsburgh pushed across two runs against a Yankees bullpen that had already survived a wild seventh, and reliever G. Soto earned the win as the Pirates stunned New York 5-3 before a crowd of 43,290.

The game was scoreless through four innings before Pittsburgh scratched out two runs in the fifth. The Yankees answered in the seventh with a three-run frame that included a homer from Rice, his 30th of the season, and solo shots from Gonzales and Gonzalez to flip a 2-0 deficit into a 3-2 lead. The Pirates, however, refused to fold. With the bases reconfigured in the 10th after a runner was placed at second, Pittsburgh manufactured the go-ahead runs to seal the win. Left on base totals told a story of their own: the Yankees stranded 24 baserunners across nine innings without delivering the knockout blow.

The two clubs also completed a makeup doubleheader earlier in the day, with New York taking the first game 2-0 behind a tidy 2:25 effort. Cody Bellinger and Jasson Dominguez each doubled in that contest, and the Yankees scored both runs in the seventh. Pittsburgh left 12 runners on base and managed nothing against New York's pitching in that shortened affair, setting the stage for the dramatic evening finale.

story.headline: SUNS GM GREGORY STANDS BEHIND BRIDGES SIGNING DESPITE TROUBLED PAST
story.deck: Brian Gregory says franchise did its homework before bringing back controversial forward Miles Bridges.
story.body:
PHOENIX — Suns general manager Brian Gregory stepped to the microphone Wednesday and delivered a firm defense of the franchise's decision to sign veteran forward Miles Bridges, acknowledging the forward's well-documented off-court troubles while insisting the organization believes those dark chapters are firmly behind him. Gregory described Bridges' past behavior as "unacceptable" but said extensive due diligence convinced the front office that the 28-year-old is a changed man ready to contribute on a contending roster.

The signing lands Bridges back in the spotlight at a moment when the NBA offseason is already crackling with noise. The Miami Heat found themselves at the center of an embarrassing blunder Wednesday after a link to a LeBron James news conference was accidentally posted before the event, a gaffe so glaring that the Winnipeg Jets hockey club couldn't resist poking fun at the Heat on social media. ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins was quick to note on air that the premature link was, in his view, no accident, suggesting the Heat organization orchestrated the leak for maximum attention.

Meanwhile, the gaming world handed the NBA its own headline when 2K Sports revealed the cover athletes for NBA 2K27. San Antonio Spurs phenom Victor Wembanyama headlines the trio, joined by Iowa women's basketball sensation Caitlin Clark and Chicago Bulls legend Derrick Rose, whose inclusion as a nostalgia pick drew immediate buzz across social media platforms. With summer league rosters still being shaped and free agency deals continuing to surface, the 2026 offseason shows no signs of quieting down anytime soon.

story.headline: ROBERTSON STAYS A STAR: DALLAS LOCKS UP 96-POINT WINGER ON ONE-YEAR DEAL
story.deck: Forward who blocked Seattle trade returns on short-term pact as long-term talks continue.
story.body:
DALLAS — Jason Robertson is staying put, at least for now. The Dallas Stars announced Wednesday they have signed their cornerstone forward to a one-year contract, keeping the 25-year-old winger in North Texas after a season in which he paced the club with 96 points and reportedly rejected a trade to the Seattle Kraken. General manager Jim Nill called Robertson a foundational piece of the franchise and made clear the organization's ambitions stretch far beyond a single season.

Nill has said publicly that securing Robertson on a long-term extension remains the primary goal, and the one-year structure of the deal signals that both sides expect to keep negotiating. Robertson, one of the most productive left wings in the Western Conference, carries enormous leverage heading into what amounts to a walk year, a dynamic that figures to dominate the Stars' front-office calendar well into the fall. Dallas cannot afford to let a player of his caliber reach open market.

Off the ice, the hockey world found a lighter moment Wednesday when the Winnipeg Jets gleefully mocked the Miami Heat's social media team after the Heat accidentally posted a link related to LeBron James during what was supposed to be NHL content. The Jets piled on with jokes that spread quickly across league accounts, a rare midsummer laugh for a sport that usually cedes July headlines to baseball and football. The Hockey Diversity Alliance, meanwhile, announced that former NFL running back Marshawn Lynch will appear as a special guest at its youth SummerFest event in Toronto this weekend.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL ROSTERS TAKE SHAPE THIS SPRING
story.deck: Several teams reshuffle signal-callers while draft picks begin their rookie journeys.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has turned into a carousel of quarterback movement, with front offices across the league scrambling to secure stable options under center before training camps open in late July. The Las Vegas Raiders agreed to terms with veteran Sam Darnold on a two-year deal worth $52 million, giving the franchise a steady hand after cycling through three starters during the 2025 season. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns parted ways with Deshaun Watson, releasing the embattled quarterback and absorbing the final dead-cap hit from the deal that once reshaped the franchise's entire salary structure.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held in Detroit last month, produced an early consensus standout in Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, who landed with the New York Giants at pick No. 3 after a flurry of pre-draft trade speculation fell apart. New York's front office believes Sanders gives the organization its most promising young passer since Eli Manning arrived in 2004. Patriots head coach Jerod Mayo called the draft class deep at edge rusher, a position New England addressed twice in the first three rounds after finishing 28th in sacks during the 2025 campaign.

Around the rest of the league, the defending Super Bowl LX champion Philadelphia Eagles locked up wide receiver DeVonta Smith on a three-year extension before he could test the open market, while the Dallas Cowboys fired offensive coordinator Brian Schottenheimer following a third consecutive first-round playoff exit. Minicamp rosters are now full and coaches are installing systems, setting the stage for what promises to be a competitive push toward the 2026 regular season opener in September.
